    MultiplicativeBasisDeformations.RaySys.Sys.centralizerRayAlgebra

    Lemma 9.2 as stated: B_χ = C_χ/𝔞_χ ≅ kQ_χ #

    integral-partial-lifts.tex (lem:centralizer-ray-algebra). Put q̂ = ∑_x q̂_x, C_χ = Cent_{A₀}(q̂), 𝔞_χ = {c ∈ C_χ : q̂c = 0} and B_χ = C_χ/𝔞_χ. "The algebra B_χ is basic and representation-finite. Its basis consists of the supporting identities and the two-sided rays of A₀, and its products define a weighted multiplication table Q_χ ... Thus B_χ = kQ_χ. If B_χ ≠ 0, it has strictly fewer nonzero basis labels than P."

    CentralizerTable.lean builds the tables Tc and Q_χ and proves the representation finiteness and the count. Here the algebras themselves: q̂ b_r = b_{r⁺} or 0, and likewise on the right (qhat_mul_b_cases, b_mul_qhat_cases), so the commutator of q̂ with a ray is ±b_{r⁺} exactly for one-sided rays (comm_b); successors of distinct rays are distinct (succ_inj). Hence C_χ is spanned by the identities, two-sided and unshiftable rays (mem_Cχ_iff, Cχ_eq_range), 𝔞_χ by the unshiftable nonidentity rays and the identities at q̂_x = 0 (mem_aχ_iff), and the quotient map C_χ → kQ_χ induces B_χ ≅ kQ_χ (Bχ_equiv, centralizerRayAlgebra).
